question.text: The difference in the oxidation state of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Xe</mi></math> between the oxidised product of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Xe</mi></math> formed on complete hydrolysis of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>XeF</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>XeF</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> is

solution.text:
Hydrolysis of XeF4 will give XeO3. This hydrolysis reaction is a redox reaction. This redox reaction is an example of disproportionation reaction.

6XeF4+12H2O→4Xe + 2XeO3+24HF+3O2

The oxidation states of Xenon in the reactant and product is 

XeO3:Xe(+6)

XeF4:Xe(+4)

Hence, the difference in oxidation state is 2.
